title: [B1 • Band 5.0] Bài 304: The Mechanical Muse: AI and Art
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 304 (LEVEL B1 • BAND 5.0)

The Mechanical Muse: Artificial Intelligence and Aesthetic Value

Paragraph 1. In May 2018, an ordinary-looking portrait of a man in historic French clothing sold at Christie's auction house in New York for $432,500—over forty times its expected price. What shocked the art world was its signature: instead of a painter's name, there was a mathematical equation. Entitled Portrait of Edmond de Belamy, the image was produced entirely by a Generative Adversarial Network (GAN), an AI model trained on 15,000 classic portraits. Many tech fans claimed machines had finally entered the last human domain: creative art.

Paragraph 2. In The Algorithmic Canvas, philosopher Dr. Julian Barnes carefully challenges this excitement. He explains that a GAN works through two competing computer programs: a 'generator' builds digital pictures out of random pixels, while a 'discriminator' compares them against real human artworks and rejects weak imitations. After millions of rounds, the generator learns to copy human style convincingly. However, Barnes insists that calling mathematical pattern-copying 'creative' confuses clever imitation with real artistic purpose.

Paragraph 3. To explain why machine art lacks genuine depth, Barnes points to human conscious experience. Human art is an act of communication born from real physical life and emotion. When Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night, his swirling brushstrokes expressed deep sadness, wonder, and spiritual longing. By contrast, a computer algorithm feels nothing, desires nothing, and possesses no physical life. It arranges statistical pixels on a screen without understanding that a pixel can represent sorrow, sunlight, or love.

Paragraph 4. Barnes also warns of serious economic risks. If businesses can generate unlimited music, stories, and visual designs at almost zero cost, the job market supporting human illustrators, composers, and writers could collapse. Worse still, because generative AI models learn strictly from historical archives, they threaten to trap culture in endless repetition—producing a safe, blended average of past tastes.

Paragraph 5. While algorithms can recombine old styles at astonishing speed, truly original art requires breaking accepted rules—an act of human courage and rebellion that mathematics alone can never imagine. As synthetic imagery spreads across media, Barnes urges society to value living human expression over effortless machine mimicry.

groups.title: Questions 1–4
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.

groups.title: Questions 5–10
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the information in the passage? Write TRUE, FALSE, or NOT GIVEN.

q1.text: What made the sale of the Portrait of Edmond de Belamy remarkable?
options: A. It was discovered in an old French museum.
B. It was the oldest portrait displayed in New York.
C. It was donated free of charge to a university.
D. It was generated by an AI program rather than a human painter.

steps: Đoạn 1: Bức tranh do mô hình AI tạo ra toàn bộ và ký tên bằng công thức toán học.
Đáp án: D.

q2.text: According to Paragraph 2, how does a GAN learn to imitate human art?
options: A. By asking human artists to fix every pixel manually
B. By making two internal programs compete against each other
C. By scanning museums with special laser cameras
D. By translating poetry lines directly into oil paint

steps: Đoạn 2: Hai chương trình cạnh tranh nhau (generator tạo ảnh, discriminator lọc đối chiếu).
Đáp án: B.

q3.text: Why does Dr. Barnes mention Van Gogh's The Starry Night?
options: A. To show that genuine art communicates real human emotion
B. To prove that computers understand nineteenth-century painting
C. To argue that famous paintings should never be scanned
D. To suggest that sadness is required to learn mathematics

steps: Đoạn 3: Nét vẽ của Van Gogh truyền tải nỗi buồn, sự kinh ngạc và khát vọng sống.
Đáp án: A.

q4.text: Which summary sentence best fits the whole passage?
options: A. Why computer software will quickly replace all art museums
B. How auction houses calculate prices for digital portraits
C. Why mathematical mimicry cannot replace authentic human creativity
D. The history of European portrait painting since the 1400s

steps: Toàn bài & Đoạn 5: Sao chép bằng thuật toán không thể thay thế sự sáng tạo có ý thức và phá cách của con người.
Đáp án: C.

q5.text: The discriminator program checks AI-generated images against real human artworks.

steps: Đoạn 2: "...a 'discriminator' compares them against real human artworks..."
Kết luận: TRUE.

q6.text: Computer algorithms will soon feel simple biological emotions like sadness and love.

steps: Đoạn 3: "...a computer algorithm feels nothing, desires nothing, and possesses no physical life."
Kết luận: FALSE.

q7.text: Museums in New York have banned AI-generated paintings from all exhibitions.

steps: Đoạn 1 & 3: Bài chỉ nhắc buổi đấu giá ở New York, không hề nói bảo tàng cấm trưng bày tranh AI.
Kết luận: NOT GIVEN.

q8.text: Free synthetic art will create higher job security for human illustrators and writers.

steps: Đoạn 4: Trái lại, thị trường việc làm nuôi sống họa sĩ và nhà văn có thể sụp đổ (could collapse).
Kết luận: FALSE.

q9.text: Creating truly original art often involves breaking established artistic rules.

steps: Đoạn 5: "...truly original art requires breaking accepted rules..."
Kết luận: TRUE.

q10.text: Dr. Julian Barnes has worked as a professional auctioneer at Christie's.

steps: Đoạn 2 & 5: Không có thông tin nói Dr. Barnes từng làm đấu giá viên.
Kết luận: NOT GIVEN.
